answer: Picture each honest agent as a jetty reaching into open water: every epoch it must anchor a running hash-thread to a public randomness beacon, signing fresh heartbeats on time. The thread is strictly serial, so one backend juggling many masks slips behind and its anchors drift out of sync; the protocol slashes any identity whose beacon-anchored thread lags. A sybil fleet therefore needs N machines each keeping its own live thread, so fakes cost real continuous wall-clock, not a one-time mint.
